assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from proglucagon processing and the incretin effect to long-acting receptor agonists, has produced a new class of drugs that transformed type 2 diabetes care and obesity treatment. The path from basic hormone biology to a validated therapy is clear and the effect on medicine is very large.
assessment.attribution: Holst established the physiology and secretion of GLP-1 and its incretin role, Drucker defined its biology and therapeutic actions, and Knudsen led the design of durable acylated analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide). Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active peptide form is real, and whether she, or others such as Habener who are not on the supplied list, should share is a genuine credit problem.
assessment.maturity: Mechanistically understood and clinically confirmed in large independent outcome trials, with a decade or more of use. Recognition is timely, since benefits keep expanding to cardiovascular and renal outcomes.
uncertainties: Allocation among Mojsov, Drucker, Holst and Knudsen is contested and the three-person limit forces a hard choice.
Whether the prize should centre on basic physiology or on the drug development is unresolved.
Details of early peptide-identification priority are from memory and not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics made it possible to control defined cell populations with light and so changed causal experimentation in neuroscience and beyond. It is a tool-level discovery with immense, broad and lasting methodological impact, and it is clearly original.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin work by Nagel, Hegemann and Bamberg gave the molecular tool; Boyden and Deisseroth made it work in neurons and extended it; Miesenböck proposed and demonstrated genetically targeted light control earlier. With six credited names, any trio omits someone with a strong claim.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated in thousands of labs for two decades, and early clinical use in vision restoration is emerging. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Many credible contributors for at most three slots, so the configuration is contested.
Clinical translation is early, so the case rests on research impact.
Relative weighting of the channelrhodopsin discovery versus neuronal implementation is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new therapeutic modality, building on a conceptual line from tumor immunology to gene-modified cells.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June engineered the second-generation receptors and led the early clinic, and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and gene-engineered T cells. Eshhar's early chimeric receptor work is not in the supplied credit, so the history may be incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and multi-year remissions are confirmed. Toxicity, solid-tumor limits and cost remain, but the principle is firmly established.
uncertainties: Omission of the earliest chimeric receptor pioneer from the supplied names.
Overlap with the checkpoint-therapy prize already given may affect how the committee frames it.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancy signals, is still being assessed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new principle of intracellular communication, signaling from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, and is relevant to secretory biology, metabolic disease, neurodegeneration and cancer. It is a clean and conceptually important discovery.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently defined the signaling pathway through Ire1 and Hac1 and later work. The two-person configuration is clear. Other contributors such as Ron or Kaufman are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Conserved from yeast to mammals, with decades of independent confirmation. Therapeutic exploitation is still developing, but the basic science is mature and widely taught.
uncertainties: Direct clinical impact is limited so far.
Contributions of mammalian UPR researchers not on the list are not assessed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The orexin/hypocretin discovery explained the cause of narcolepsy type 1 and identified a specific neuropeptide circuit stabilizing wakefulness. It has led to orexin-receptor antagonists and agonists in development, and it has strong physiological and clinical coherence.
assessment.attribution: Sakurai and Yanagisawa identified orexins and the receptors; de Lecea and Kilduff independently discovered hypocretins; Mignot's canine genetics showed the receptor mutation in narcolepsy. Priority is shared across several groups, which makes a fair three-way split difficult.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed, with approved antagonists for insomnia and orexin agonists in clinical development. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Parallel discovery by two groups complicates attribution.
Agonist therapies are not yet approved at the time of my knowledge, so translational maturity is partial.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 work defined a distinct way for oncogenes to act, by blocking cell death, and established the apoptosis regulatory machinery. It led to BH3 mimetics such as venetoclax, which give a complete bench-to-bedside story.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the cloning and characterization of the BCL-2 family; Vaux showed its cell-death-inhibiting function in vivo and in cooperation with Myc. Strasser is a strong contributor to the family's biology. Tsujimoto, who cloned the translocation, is not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and clinically validated in CLL and other leukemias, with a long track record.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the earlier apoptosis prize may affect committee appetite.
Omitted contributors such as the original translocation cloners may weaken the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, which changed the course of a severe fatal childhood disease. It also demonstrated the broader power of splice-modulating oligonucleotides.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and the ASO target, and Bennett led the antisense chemistry and drug development at Ionis. This is a clear two-person configuration, though Biogen and clinical investigators also played a role.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016, with long-term outcomes and now other SMN-directed therapies. Recognition would be timely, though fundamental novelty may be judged narrower than other candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as a disease-specific therapeutic advance or a broad conceptual one.
Role of the original antisense oligonucleotide pioneers is not covered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR signaling revealed the central pathway linking nutrient and growth-factor cues to cell growth and metabolism, with consequences for cancer, aging, immunosuppression and metabolic disease.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically and defined its function, while Schreiber's chemical genetics with rapamycin and FKBP12 helped identify the target. Sabatini's work on mTORC1 regulation is large, but I leave him out given the difficult allocation and the uncertain fairness of a three-person set.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed and clinically relevant, as rapalogs are in use, though cancer and aging applications remain more limited than hoped.
uncertainties: Credit among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and other TOR pioneers is unsettled.
Clinical consequences are narrower than the basic biology suggests.
